outline.chapter_title: Foundations of Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces the fundamental paradigms of Reinforcement Learning (RL) as applied to Large Language Models (LLMs), establishing the context for why specific optimization algorithms are necessary for scaling intelligence.
subtopics: Role of RL in scaling LLMs for reasoning, mathematics, and programming
Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO): Mechanics, clipping mechanisms, and the value model burden
Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO): Eliminating the value model via group-based relative advantages
Standard Notation: Autoregressive policies, sequence likelihoods, and reward verifiers

outline.chapter_title: The Problem of Token-Level Optimization in GRPO
outline.description: This chapter explores the theoretical and practical limitations of current state-of-the-art algorithms like GRPO, identifying why token-level importance sampling leads to training instability.
subtopics: Off-policy learning and the necessity of clipping in large-scale RL
The Principle of Importance Sampling: Correcting distributional mismatch
The 'Ill-posed' nature of GRPO: Why token-level weights fail to correct distributions
High-variance noise accumulation and the phenomenon of catastrophic model collapse
The Core Principle: Aligning the unit of reward with the unit of optimization

outline.description: This chapter presents the core contribution of the paper: the GSPO algorithm, detailing its mathematical formulation and why it provides a more stable learning signal.
subtopics: The GSPO Objective: Moving to sequence-level importance ratios
Mathematical derivation of the sequence-level importance ratio $s_i(θ)$
Length Normalization: Controlling variance and ensuring unified numerical ranges
Gradient Analysis: Comparing the gradient weights of GSPO vs. GRPO
Eliminating instability: How equal weighting of tokens stabilizes training

outline.description: This chapter delves into a more flexible variant of the proposed algorithm and provides a rigorous mathematical comparison between the different objectives.
subtopics: GSPO-token: Enabling fine-grained, token-wise advantage adjustment
Mathematical formulation of GSPO-token and its gradient derivation
Theoretical Equivalence: Proving numerical identity between GSPO and GSPO-token in standard settings
Applications in multi-turn RL and complex advantage customization

outline.description: The final chapter discusses the experimental results that validate GSPO, its specific advantages for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, and its benefits for production infrastructure.
subtopics: Benchmark Results: Performance on AIME'24, LiveCodeBench, and CodeForces
The Paradox of Clipping: Why clipping more tokens results in higher training efficiency
MoE Stability: Solving expert-activation volatility and the obsolescence of Routing Replay
Infrastructure Benefits: Tolerance for precision discrepancies between training and inference engines
Conclusion: GSPO as a foundation for scalable RL training
